items.title: Stock Prices, Earnings and Cashflows: The AI Effect plays through!
items.summary: In a post at the end of August 2026, I talked about interest rates in 2026 and marveled at the capacity of equities to keep rising in the face of rising rates.
items.finding: I argued that the resilience of stocks during the year could be traced to higher-than-expected earnings being reported by companies in 2026, and a concurrent increase in expected earnings in 2027 and 2028.

items.title: Investor Sentiment and Stock Market Returns in Nigeria
items.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
items.summary: The Nigerian bourse is characterized by continual volatility and unpredictability that traditional macroeconomic models have failed to sufficiently explain this phenomenon.
items.finding: Nevertheless, the GARCH model showed positive and significant volatility persistence, implying that past volatility contributed to current market volatility.

items.title: Social media sentiment, behavioral biases, and abnormal returns: evidence from Indonesian Non-Cyclical Consumer Stocks
items.summary: Social media has become an important source of information for investors, while stock price anomalies continue to challenge market efficiency.
items.finding: The reported main model shows positive and statistically significant associations for social media sentiment and herding, while firm size is also significant while included as a control variable.

items.title: Getting Bonds (and Diversification) Wrong
items.summary: One of the most common views expressed in financial markets at present seems to be that bonds (particularly the government variety) are no longer an effective diversifier when held alongside equities in a multi-asset portfolio.
items.finding: We take recent returns, build a story to explain them and then extrapolate.

items.title: The depositary of last resort
items.summary: What are the consequences of making central bank deposits accessible to actors beyond the banking sector?
items.finding: At the same time, retail borrowers seeking liquidity support from the Bank during the crisis preferred receiving loan proceeds in the form of cash rather than deposits.

items.title: The Financial Premium
items.summary: ABSTRACT We show that bonds issued by financial firms have higher spreads than bonds issued by industrial firms with the same rating and maturity, a difference that we refer to as the financial premium.
items.finding: Over the period 1987 to 2020, in the United States, this premium is 43 basis points on average, with the premium higher for lower ratings, higher during financial crises, and increasing in bond beta.

items.title: Effect Of Share Repurchase Programs on Shareholder Wealth: A Systematic Literature Review
items.publisher: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
items.venue: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
items.summary: Stock buybacks, or share repurchase programs, are a corporate financial tool that has been an increasingly significant and influential financial approach to maximising shareholder wealth and capital allocation.
items.finding: The results show that buyback announcements tend to have a positive short-term abnormal return which are indicative of positive investor responses and reflective of the effects.

items.title: The Macroeconomics of Irrational Exuberance, Mathematical Microstructures of the VIX, and Prospect Theory: A Behavioral and Empirical Synthesis
items.summary: This paper investigates the cyclical architecture of asset price bubbles and the behavioral microstructures that accelerate systemic market panics.
items.finding: Finally, we evaluate systematic quantitative risk-targeting protocols and discretionary portfolio hedging overlays as necessary mechanisms to defend institutional capital against procyclical reflexivity loops.

items.title: Feedback and Contagion through Distressed Competition
items.summary: ABSTRACT Firms tend to compete more aggressively when facing financial distress.
items.finding: The feedback effect represents a novel source of financial distress costs associated with leverage, which helps explain the negative profitability‐leverage relation across industries.

items.title: Financial mismatch and stock mispricing in China: Industry-year averages and firm-level differences

A Comparison between Estimating the Required Rate of Return in Market Value and Within the Framework of (ROI) and its Impact on the Fair Value of Shares - A Comparative Study of Iraqi Industrial Companies for the Period (2015-2024)
items.venue: Global Academic Journal of Economics and Business
items.summary: This research aims to assess the effectiveness of using the book value and market value frameworks to estimate the implied required rate of return (Ke), examining their subsequent impact on determining the fair value of common stocks and comparing their effects.
items.finding: Its most important findings have profound implications for institutional investors, financial analysts, and regulatory bodies seeking robust valuation methodologies less susceptible to anomalies in temporary market movements.

items.title: Generative AI and Firm Values
items.summary: ABSTRACT How do recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) affect firm value?
items.finding: We construct the first measure of firms' workforce exposures to Generative AI and show that an “Artificial‐Minus‐Human” portfolio earned 5% in the two weeks following the release of ChatGPT.

items.title: The impact of corporate information disclosure ambiguity on investor sentiment: Evidence from stock forum text analysis
Competing digital money
items.summary: We study competition between two payment instruments: bank deposits and digital platform tokens.
items.finding: When new payment service providers (PSPs) enter and compete for consumers, they soften competition for merchants: incumbent intermediaries then charge merchants higher fees and earn higher profits.

items.title: Communicating Quantitative and AI-Driven Investment Strategies: Narrative, Interpretation, and Governance
Machine Learning Classification and Portfolio Construction: Does the Loss Function Matter?
Targeted Philanthropy: Evidence from M&As
items.summary: ABSTRACT I show how firms optimize the allocation of charitable funds around investments that require external stakeholder support, such as mergers and acquisitions.
items.finding: Targeted donations that encourage blockholder reciprocity and employee commitment are associated with better deal performance through decreased merger premiums and lower integration costs.

items.title: Directing the Labor Market: Shared Directors and Employee Flows
items.summary: Using résumé data on over 20 million U.S. workers, we find that the flow of employees between a pair of firms sharply drops by about 20% during periods in which the firms share a board director.
items.finding: Moreover, we find more connected firms have lower rates of internal promotion and no improvements in employee satisfaction.

items.title: Central Bank Economic Transparency and Managerial Learning
items.summary: Central banks increasingly disclose their private information regarding the economy’s current and future state (CBET).
items.finding: Consistent with CBET shifting investors’ collection and pricing of aggregate-level (where managers do not have an information advantage) toward firm-level (where managers do have an information advantage) information, we find that CBET reduces managers’…

items.title: Creation after destruction? Financial intermediation and firm entry after bank cleanups
items.summary: We study a large and unanticipated bank cleanup in India after prolonged zombie lending under regulatory forbearance.
items.finding: We further find a decline in the dispersion of total factor productivity in regions with stronger financial intermediation, consistent with a reduction in misallocation in such areas.

items.title: Flow‐Driven ESG Returns
items.summary: ABSTRACT I show that the recent returns to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing are strongly driven by price impact from flows toward ESG portfolios.
items.finding: I show that every dollar flowing toward a representative ESG portfolio increases the market value of ESG stocks by $0.8.

items.title: Stakeholder Management and Communication in the Total Portfolio Approach
Stock Market Liberalization and Institutional Investor Clique Behavior: Evidence from China
items.publisher: International Journal of Advanced AI Applications
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced AI Applications
items.summary: This study examines how stock market liberalization affects the clique behavior of domestic institutional investors, distinguishing hotspot clustering from value clustering.
items.finding: We find that stock market liberalization significantly reduces hotspot clustering while promoting value clustering.

items.title: Is the business of frontier AI companies selling tokens? Value capture and equity prices
items.summary: We examine business models that could support frontier AI companies' valuations and the public evidence of plans to earn income beyond selling model access.
items.finding: We discuss how these arrangements relate to firm boundaries and value capture.

items.title: Investor attention and GCC stock market connectedness during the first wave of COVID-19: evidence using Google trends and VIX
items.summary: This study investigates the behavioral determinants of financial market connectedness in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) during the first wave of COVID-19.
items.finding: Given fundamental controls, Granger causality tests show unidirectional precedence from GTR to TCI in bivariate specifications.

items.title: From Models to Workflows: Communicating Agentic AI in Asset Management
Explaining Risk to Boards: Translating Quantitative Models into Fiduciary Dialogue
SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions
items.summary: As option markets grow and AI advances, agentic systems for option trading are gaining increasing attention.
items.finding: We also document an asymmetric role of news: news improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning reduces out-of-sample return from 18.3% to -2.7%.

items.title: Carbon Footprints and Indonesia Market Dynamics: The Risk-Mitigation Role of Artificial Intelligence Innovation
items.venue: Business Innovation Management and Entrepreneurship Journal (BIMANTARA)
items.summary: Climate transition has increased investors' concerns about carbon risk, yet evidence remains limited on how firms' technological capabilities shape market responses, particularly in emerging markets.
items.finding: The results show that carbon risk is marginally associated with lower stock returns and increases stock volatility, while AI innovation significantly weakens the positive effect of carbon risk on stock volatility but has no direct effect on stock returns.

items.title: The Rise of Finfluencers and Their Impact on Individual Investment Decisions in India: A Regulatory Perspective with Reference to SEBI Guidelines
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary: The rapid rise of financial influencers popularly known as finfluencers has been one of the most visible developments in India’s financial ecosystem in the last decade.
items.finding: However, their growing influence has also raised significant regulatory, ethical, and economic concerns.

items.title: The Impact of Social Media Influence on Investor Behavior and Purchase Intention in the Indian Stock Market
items.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
items.summary: In spite of the fast rise in participation of retail investors in the Indian stock market through social media, the available body of literature on the topic has not tried to disentangle which of the above-mentioned elements of 'social media influence' drive investment actions.
items.finding: However, the regression analysis revealed a model to be significant with F(5,196)= 25.410, p < .001, which accounted for 39.3 percent of the variance in Purchase Intention.

items.title: Pricing Repurchase Promises: Expected Execution and Investor Beliefs
items.summary: Using 10,752 Chinese announcements, I construct an expanding out-of-sample execution forecast from current firm and plan information and distinguish it from historical execution reputation.
items.finding: I study how investors price expected repurchase delivery and what actual purchases reveal beyond that expectation.

items.title: Inflation, DER, PER, and TATO as Determinants of Capital Gains for Indonesian Telecommunication Companies (2020-2025)
items.venue: JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES SOCIAL SCIENCES AND BUSINESS (JHSSB)
items.summary: Telecommunications sector stocks are widely regarded as stable, defensive investments, attractive to investors due to consistent capital gains and reliable dividend yields.
items.finding: Jointly, these four predictors explain 9% of the variance in capital gains and exert a collectively significant influence.

items.title: Safety Research and the Allocation of Frontier Compute
items.summary: During a frontier takeoff period, an AI lab splits a committed stock of compute among capability research, safety research, and customers, and a regulator limits both the services customers lose and how long any capability can be delayed.
items.finding: Varying the calibration shows how delay costs, additional safety learning, and service valuation move it; in the baseline, it rises with the service budget.
